_comment: Every structural claim this project has made about a field, and what happened when it was tested under rule 18. The owner's requirement: the final Phase 2 report leads with this ledger, before any coverage number, because it says more about whether the dataset can be trusted than category counts do. A claim is only listed once it has been TESTED — an untested claim is not a finding and does not belong here. INWARD-FACING CLAIMS are tracked here too, and are the most dangerous class: a claim about our own criteria reads as introspection but is an empirical claim about the data. Two of the falsifications are of this kind, and both were live on the site.
_schema: status: falsified | survived. Each entry names the sub-areas, which were probed, what was found, and where the correction lives.

claims.claim: Marketing's independent practitioners publish in newsletters and blogs; the video supply is vendor-hosted.
claims.found: Alex Cattoni (848 uploads, a real copywriting curriculum), Pat Flynn (four 70-85 minute affiliate workshops) and 30 Minutes to President's Club all publish substantially in video. The standing note built on the claim was retired at 6/9, 67%.
claims.survives: The narrow form: Harry Dry has 4 uploads, Seth Godin 7, copyhackers and backlinko unresolvable, and the SEO end really is vendor-hosted.

claims.claim: No usable first-aid teaching exists on video; the certifying bodies use YouTube for campaigns.
claims.found: PrepMedic, a critical-care flight paramedic with 353 uploads and 44 long-form bystander-first-aid videos, found on the first probe of the clinician end.
claims.survives: The institutional claim: certification needs hands-on assessment, so the bodies that certify treat the course as the product and video as its marketing.

claims.found: Brand Master Academy: 39-63 minute interviews with April Dunford, Bobby Moesta, Blair Enns, Laura Ries.

claims.claim: practitioner, credentialed and cites-research are near-universal in some domains because of OUR inclusion rules — 'we do not list someone who explains a skill they have never practised'.
subAreas: whether any listed creator lacks the badge
whether the share is uniform across domains
claims.found: 29 of 196 creators carry no practitioner badge, so it is not a requirement. Measured across domains it runs 100% (marketing, business, fitness, programming, productivity) to 14% (philosophy). An inclusion rule would be near-uniform. credentialed runs 70% (relationships) to 0% (marketing); cites-research 71% (philosophy) to 0% (programming). All three track the subject, not our preference.
claims.survives: A real but secondary editorial preference for qualifications in relationships, which is why that one entry is 'mixed' rather than 'field'.
claims.correctionIn: data/domain-notes.json corrected — 15 entries reclassified and moved to category pages; the colophon section rewritten
claims.note: The worst of the four: never probed at all when made, repeated in every batch report from 17 to 25, and shipped to visitors as a claim about our own rigour.

claims.claim: Independent, credentialed, educational addiction content is genuinely scarce.
claims.found: The clinician end is ASAM: 49 uploads, archived since February 2021, conference plenaries addressed to physicians. Five other clinician handles do not resolve.

claims.claim: No conversion-optimization teaching catalogue exists on video.
claims.found: All four probed before the claim was written — the first gap documented in the right order. Nudgestock recorded as a near-miss and not mapped: adjacent subject, not the same one.

claims.claim: No credible critic of the relationship-advice field exists on video.
subAreas: credentialed clinicians critiquing the content industry
claims.found: Mickey Atkins is the near-miss — credentialed, with a substantive Dr. Amen debunk — but her critical work is a small part of a catalogue that is mostly reality-television commentary, so the slot would be thin. Rule 11 applies.
claims.survives: The claim, on rule 11 grounds rather than absence.

claims.claim: No credible critic of commercialised philosophy exists on video.
claims.found: Philosophy Tube read rather than counted: 15 of 50 recent uploads over twenty minutes, but the subject is political and social essay, not criticism of philosophy content.

claims.claim: A creator appears under a skill only when their work supports it — typically two to four skills, never more than six. (Stated on the colophon to visitors, and as the default in rule 4.)
claims.madeAt: phase 1 brief, shipped on the colophon in batch 22
subAreas: the actual distribution of mappings per creator
whether the design intent was ever met
claims.found: The median is 1 and the mean 1.47. 62% of creators have exactly ONE mapping; only 38% fall in the claimed two-to-four band. The ratio was measured at 1.58 back at 143 creators and has DRIFTED DOWN since — so the claim got steadily more wrong and was never re-run.
claims.survives: The 'never more than six' half, and the scope rule itself. 2-4 was always a design intent in rule 4, not a description of the dataset; the error was restating an intent to visitors as a fact.
claims.correctionIn: js/views/colophon.js — the rule now says most appear under one, and the coverage section computes the median rather than asserting it
claims.note: Second inward-facing claim to fail, and the same shape as the badge one: cheap to query, never queried.

claims.claim: The site keeps two things in your browser: plan progress, and whether you dismissed the survey question.
claims.found: Five distinct stores, not two: theme preference, plan progress, categories seen this session, whether the form endpoint exists, and the survey dismissal state. I grepped localStorage when writing the sentence and never looked at sessionStorage — the same partial-search error as the outward findings, at the smallest possible scale, one exchange after naming the pattern.
claims.survives: That nothing leaves the device and nothing reaches us. Both still true.
claims.correctionIn: index.html footer now names the kinds and states no count; validate.mjs holds a registry and fails on any undisclosed store
claims.note: Caught by the enforcement written in the same batch, not by review. The check found its author's error within minutes of existing.
